claims.text: ``--quick`` runs this one. It is the probe that would have caught both real incidents on day one, so if only one probe can be afforded, it is this one.
claims.why: The claim refers to real incidents not present in this chunk; the assignment of QUICK_PROBE is observed but the justification cannot be verified.

claims.text: One (lane, probe) outcome. Carries WHICH check failed, not just that one did.
claims.why: ProbeResult includes failed_check field to indicate which check failed.

claims.text: Name of the failed deterministic check (``nonce_absent``, ``anchored_on_decoy``, ...). Empty when the checker was never reached.
claims.why: failed_check field is documented and defaults to empty string.

claims.text: Machine reason from the transport (``not_authenticated``, ``connect_failed``, ...). Empty on ``ok``/``wrong_answer``.
claims.why: reason field is documented and defaults to empty string.

claims.text: Did a prompt actually reach a model? ``unavailable`` means it did not.
claims.why: asked property returns True if status != 'unavailable'.

claims.text: This run's result against the trailing history for the same triple.
claims.why: Comparison dataclass holds vendor, model, probe, and comparison fields.

claims.text: Counts that keep "could not ask" apart from "answer was wrong". ``asked`` and ``could_not_ask`` are separate top-level keys and ``by_status`` reports every member of the closed vocabulary individually. There is deliberately no combined "failures" number: a single number is exactly where the two get merged.
claims.why: summary() returns separate keys 'asked', 'could_not_ask', 'by_status', and does not combine them.

claims.text: Non-zero only when a previously-passing LIVENESS probe now fails. Not "something is red": a lane that has never passed is not a regression, and an unavailable lane is not a failure at all. A quality regression is printed but does not page anyone -- see the module docstring.
claims.why: exit_code returns 1 only if regressions('liveness') is non-empty; regressions filter by regressed flag.

claims.text: One vendor endpoint plus the callable that asks it a question. ``ask`` is ``(prompt: str, timeout_s: float) -> VendorReply``. Injecting it is what lets the whole runner be tested with fakes and no network: the tests never construct an adapter, never touch a CLI and never open a socket.
claims.why: Lane dataclass has ask field of type Callable; docstring describes its purpose.

claims.text: ``adapter`` is the seat ``ask`` was bound from, when there was one. It is carried for ONE reason: :func:`live_egress_lanes` has to hand something to :func:`session.live_egress_seats`, and a bare closure is not classifiable. Nothing in the runner reads it -- the canary still calls ``ask`` and only ``ask``, so a fake lane stays a fake lane.
claims.why: adapter field is optional and documented as unused by runner.

claims.text: Resolve a vendor CLI to something ``CreateProcess`` can actually launch. On Windows a node CLI ships as an extensionless shell script beside a ``.exe``/``.cmd`` shim, and only the shim is launchable without a shell. Preferring the native ``.exe`` also skips the ``.cmd`` layer entirely -- the layer that truncated a multi-line argv and started all of this. (The prompt still goes on stdin regardless; the arrival probe is what proves that end to end rather than asserting it.) Returns ``name`` unchanged when nothing is found, so the spawn fails as ``not_on_path`` -> ``unavailable`` instead of guessing.
claims.why: resolve_exe iterates over candidates with .exe, .cmd, .bat, then name; returns first found or name unchanged.

claims.text: Two overrides every canary adapter needs, and nothing else.

The council's data-notice preamble is for model-written evidence. A canary prompt is generated in this file and carries none -- and the preamble would sit AHEAD of the arrival nonce, destroying the head position that probe measures. So the probe body goes out verbatim.
claims.why: assemble method simply returns prompt unchanged.

claims.text: argv returns list with first element resolved via resolve_exe.
claims.why: argv method in _CanaryAdapterMixin calls resolve_exe on argv[0].

observations.what: ProbeResult dataclass has no validation for failed_check or reason fields beyond defaults.
Comparison dataclass has no validation for regressed or slower fields.
CanaryRun.summary() counts liveness_failures and quality_failures based on severity and status in FAILING_STATUSES, but FAILING_STATUSES is not defined in this chunk.
CanaryRun.exit_code() calls self.regressions('liveness'), which depends on regressed flag in Comparison; the flag's assignment is not in this chunk.
resolve_exe returns name unchanged if no candidate found; this may hide configuration errors.
